text: Milo et al.'s 2002 Science paper 'Network Motifs: Simple Building Blocks of Complex Networks' is best known for which contribution?
choices: Demonstrating the repressilator's oscillatory dynamics using ODE simulations
Deriving zero-order ultrasensitivity in covalent modification cycles
Introducing the original statistical framework for detecting network motifs, applied across E. coli, yeast, neural, and web networks
Proposing the Watts-Strogatz small-world network model
explanation: Milo et al. (2002) introduced the original statistical framework -- comparing subgraph counts to randomized networks with the same degree sequence -- for identifying overrepresented network motifs, and applied it broadly to gene regulation, yeast, neural, and web networks. Repressilator dynamics were modeled by Elowitz & Leibler, zero-order ultrasensitivity was derived by Goldbeter & Koshland (1981), and the small-world model is due to Watts & Strogatz, not Milo et al.
